features.name: Damascus Sulcus
features.description: Damascus Sulcus is one of the four great tiger stripes cut across Enceladus's south polar terrain. The fracture is part of the warm vent system that sprays water vapor, ice grains, salts, and organic-rich material from the moon's buried ocean into space.

details.label: Role
details.value: Primary south polar vent fissure

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 76.90 deg S, 285.87 deg W

details.label: Map cue
details.value: One of the nearly parallel dark-blue fractures crossing the south pole

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Cassini flew through plume material from the tiger stripes and directly sampled grains linked to Enceladus's ocean.

features.name: Baghdad Sulcus
features.description: Baghdad Sulcus is one of Enceladus's most important active fractures. Saturn's gravity flexes the moon during each orbit, stressing the icy shell and helping this long canyon leak heat and ocean-derived particles from below.

details.label: Heat source
details.value: Tidal flexing from Saturn's gravity

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 86.90 deg S, 230.54 deg W

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Near-polar tiger stripe anchor deep in the south polar terrain

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Plume output changes over Enceladus's orbit as the fissures are squeezed and relaxed.

features.name: Cairo Sulcus
features.description: Cairo Sulcus is another of the named tiger stripes that slice through the young south polar cap. Its sharp walls and blue-toned fresh ice mark a place where Enceladus's crust has been pulled open instead of left to collect ancient craters.

details.label: Terrain age
details.value: Geologically young compared with Enceladus's older cratered regions

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 80.37 deg S, 154.48 deg W

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The south polar terrain is so geologically young that it lacks the heavy cratering seen across most of Enceladus.

features.name: Alexandria Sulcus
features.description: Alexandria Sulcus completes the set of four prominent tiger stripes named by the IAU. Together with Damascus, Baghdad, and Cairo, it forms the distinctive south polar fracture belt that makes Enceladus one of the most active icy worlds known.

details.label: Feature family
details.value: One of the four major named tiger stripe sulci

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 79.41 deg S, 137.56 deg W

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Parallel south polar fracture near the other tiger stripes

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The four tiger stripes were named for places from The Arabian Nights, matching Enceladus's naming theme.

features.name: South Polar Plume Curtain
features.description: A curtain of icy jets rises from vents along the tiger stripes, feeding Saturn's broad E ring with fresh particles. The plume is the reason Enceladus is such a powerful astrobiology target: it lets spacecraft sample ocean material without drilling through the ice.

details.label: Plume height
details.value: Hundreds of kilometres above the surface

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Enceladus is one of the few worlds where a spacecraft has sampled ocean material without landing.

features.name: South Polar Terrain
features.description: The south polar terrain is Enceladus's active engine room. It is warmer, smoother, and less cratered than the surrounding icy shell, with ridges and fractures arranged around the plume-bearing tiger stripes.

details.label: Science value
details.value: Connects surface fractures, internal heat, and the subsurface ocean

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright polar cap surrounding the tiger stripe fracture belt

features.name: Sarandib Planitia
features.description: Sarandib Planitia is a broad, smoother plain that contrasts with Enceladus's older battered terrains. Its relatively clean surface points to resurfacing by tectonics, frost deposition, or warm ice movement long after the moon first formed.

details.label: Surface character
details.value: Smoother and less cratered than ancient terrain

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: On Enceladus, smooth plains likely record episodes when warm ice welled up and spread across the surface before freezing solid again.

features.name: Diyar Planitia
features.description: Diyar Planitia is a bright icy plain marked by fractures and relatively few impact scars. It helps tell the larger Enceladus story: this moon has repeatedly refreshed parts of its shell instead of preserving one uniformly ancient surface.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Enceladus reflects nearly all sunlight that reaches it, making it one of the brightest natural objects in the Solar System.

features.name: Samarkand Sulci
features.description: Samarkand Sulci is a long fracture system that runs far from the south polar geyser zone. It shows that Enceladus's icy shell has been globally stressed, cracked, and renewed, not merely disturbed at the active pole.

details.label: Approximate length
details.value: About 360 km

details.label: IAU coordinate anchor
details.value: 30.00 deg N, 327.50 deg W

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Samarkand Sulci spans a huge fraction of a moon only about 504 kilometres across.

features.name: Harran Sulci
features.description: Harran Sulci is a broad region of grooved terrain that bounds Diyar Planitia to the north and east. Voyager images showed it as sinuous mountainous ridges, while Cassini later revealed a more complex ridge belt with scarps and cross-cutting fractures.

details.label: Approximate length
details.value: About 276 km

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 26.70 deg N, 237.60 deg W

details.label: Terrain role
details.value: Forms a tectonic boundary around Diyar Planitia

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Researchers have compared the ridge belt texture to fold belts, a sign that Enceladus's icy crust has been compressed and warped.

features.name: Labtayt Sulci
features.description: Labtayt Sulci is a system of deep fractures seen in detail by Cassini during its February 2005 Enceladus flyby. It cuts across the boundary of the south polar terrain, where stresses in the ice appear to have forced the crust open.

details.label: Approximate size
details.value: About 162 km long, 4 km wide, and 1 km deep

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 28.00 deg S, 284.00 deg W

details.label: Science value
details.value: Shows how the south polar terrain connects to older tectonic structures outside the active tiger stripes

features.name: Bassorah Fossa
features.description: Bassorah Fossa is a long, narrow tectonic depression in Enceladus's northern terrain. It adds another piece to the moon's global stress pattern, showing that faulting and extension are not limited to the active south pole.

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 45.40 deg N, 6.30 deg W

details.label: Feature type
details.value: Fossa: a long, narrow depression or trough

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for Bassorah, a location from The Arabian Nights

features.name: Daryabar Fossa
features.description: Daryabar Fossa is an east-west trending trough first seen by Voyager 2 and later sampled in higher resolution by Cassini. Its relationship with Isbanir Fossa suggests linked faulting, offset troughs, and possible spreading-style deformation.

details.label: Approximate length
details.value: About 201 km

details.label: Approximate shape
details.value: About 400 m deep and 4 km wide

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 9.70 deg N, 359.10 deg W

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Daryabar means Seaside in Persian, matching its Arabian Nights naming source.

features.name: Isbanir Fossa
features.description: Isbanir Fossa is a north-south trending scarp that cuts across nearby troughs such as Daryabar Fossa. Topographic studies describe it as a west-dipping scarp, and the offsets around it make it a candidate strike-slip or transform-style fault.

details.label: Approximate length
details.value: About 132 km

details.label: Relief
details.value: About 300 m tall

details.label: Coordinate anchor
details.value: Converted from 12.60 deg N, 354.00 deg W

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Named for the home of Fakir Taj in The Arabian Nights

features.name: Dunyazad
features.description: Dunyazad is a named crater in Enceladus's northern terrains. Craters like this are useful contrast points against the youthful south pole because they preserve the older impact history that active regions have erased.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 30.8 km

details.label: IAU coordinate anchor
details.value: 41.51 deg N, 202.04 deg W

details.label: Name origin
details.value: Sister of Shahrazad in The Arabian Nights

features.name: Morgiana
features.description: Morgiana is a smaller crater near Dunyazad in the older northern hemisphere. Its preserved rim helps visitors read Enceladus as a world of contrasts: ancient crater fields in some regions and fresh, active ice at the south pole.

details.label: Diameter
details.value: About 15.4 km

details.label: IAU coordinate anchor
details.value: 31.75 deg N, 196.17 deg W

details.label: Name origin
details.value: The clever slave girl from Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
